newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul says N.Korean food crisis avoidable.
newsitem.headline: Seoul says N.Korean food crisis avoidable.

text.p: North Korea can avoid a serious food crisis as it has an estimated 1.22 million tonnes of food in stock to help the communist state survive until harvest, the South Korean unification ministry said on Tuesday.
The ministry estimated that up to June North Korea had secured 4.35 million tonnes of food from last year's harvest, imports and international aid, of which it had consumed 3.13 million tonnes.

"From July to this year's harvest, there is an estimated 75,000-tonne food shortage, thus it is forecast that an extreme crisis can be avoided," said a statement by the Ministry of National Unification.

The ministry estimated that the Stalinist state would need 1.57 million tonnes of food to see the country until October and added 275,000 tonnes of food was pledged to the North through international aid.

"The food shortage among North Korean residents during the first half of the year seemed to have been caused by a breakdown in the food distribution system and food rationing provided according to social class, rather then a shortage of supplies," the statement said.
North Korea has been suffering from acute shortages after two consecutive years of massive floods.
On Saturday, U.N. Undersecretary General Yasushi Akashi, who recently visited North Korea, called for additional aid to the impoverished nation.
He said although foreign food aids have somehow eased the North's food shortage, it still needed between 700,000 and 800,000 tonnes of food.
The U.N. aims to collect $126 million worth of food contributions during the year to March 1998, of which 40 percent has been attained, Akashi said. The South has already pledged $16 million.
